properties.description:
Fifth and last theme of the triage-fixes increment, and the only one whose SHAPE was undecided when it started.

⭐ THE RECONNAISSANCE DECIDED IT, AND IT RULED OUT THE OBVIOUS ANSWER FIRST: only 2 of this design's 2,367 nodes carry `created_at`. So "what did this session write" is NOT computable from timestamps and never was — the design has no clock, by design. Anthony chose the baseline that IS computable: the COMMITTED EXPORT. `loop_status(since_export: true)` reports the nodes the durable record does not hold yet, and the gaps and defects standing on them.

WHY THAT BASELINE IS ARGUABLY BETTER THAN A CLOCK RATHER THAN MERELY AVAILABLE: the export is the only copy that survives losing the gitignored graph directory, so "what is not in the record" is the question with consequences. A session that ends with its work unexported has lost it whatever the timestamps say.

⚠️ AND THE FLAW IS STATED ON EVERY ANSWER, in `note`, rather than left to be discovered: THE BASELINE MOVES whenever anyone exports — including this session mid-flight, and another seat on a shared graph. It is not a session boundary; it is a record boundary that usually coincides with one.

OFF BY DEFAULT, on Anthony's second ruling: it reads and parses the committed export, and the ordinary orientation call has no reason to pay for that. The unscoped reply is byte-identical to before. That mirrors `sync_debt`, which already defers its expensive half until something has moved.

SCOPED HONESTLY, AND ONLY WHERE IT CAN BE: only the two debt classes carrying `affected_ids` — gaps and structural defects — can be attributed to ground, so only they are scoped. EVERY OTHER COUNTER STAYS DESIGN-WIDE and the note says so, because a scoped answer that quietly dropped the rest would be the "nothing is owed" failure this project refuses everywhere else.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT THAT MATTERS MOST is the empty baseline: no readable record and a genuinely new design look IDENTICAL from here, so the answer says which it cannot tell rather than implying a clean session. Mutation-checked — removing that branch fails exactly that one test, and ignoring the baseline entirely fails exactly the fully-recorded case.

MEASURED END TO END through a real server over stdio, on a scratch graph: create, export, create one more, ask — `unexported_nodes: 1`, sample `['req:new']`, and the unscoped call omits the block entirely.

📌 AND F24 ARRIVED ON ME WHILE PROVING IT: the MCP client caches tool schemas for the session, so the newly added `since_export` was unusable from the session that added it — the server accepted the field and the client sent it as a string. That is the same class as the latent-surface dead end fixed this morning, and it is why the verification was done by driving the binary directly.
properties.name: loop_status gains since_export — debt on ground the committed record does not hold yet, which is the closest a clockless design can get to what this session owes
